facts.fact_text: The applicants in all three applications (nos. 69483/13, 76319/13, and 30456/14) were members of a political group called the Public Chamber (İctimai Palata).
As members of the Public Chamber (İctimai Palata), the applicants planned to hold several assemblies in 2012 in Baku.
The applicants in application no. 69483/13 planned an assembly in the form of a picketing, to be held on 22 April 2012.
The applicants in application no. 76319/13 planned an assembly in the form of a march followed by a meeting, to be held on 22 April 2012.
The applicant in application no. 30456/14 planned an assembly in the form of a march, to be held on 13 October 2012.
The purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was to demand the removal of unwritten restrictions placed on the freedom of assembly.
The purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was to demand political reforms.
The purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was to demand freedom for political prisoners.
According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included demanding new parliamentary elections.
According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included demanding political reforms.
According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included demanding freedom for political prisoners.

According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included demanding protection of the right to freedom of assembly.
According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included protesting against corruption.
According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included protesting against violation of property rights.
The purpose of the assembly planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14 was to demand early elections to the Parliament of Azerbaijan.
By a letter of 18 April 2012, the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13.

By a letter of 18 April 2012, the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 at any of the three locations proposed by the applicants.

By a letter of 10 October 2012, the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the assembly planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14 at the location indicated by the applicant.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), in its letter of 18 April 2012, proposed another location for the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13, namely the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail district, on the outskirts of Baku.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), in its letter of 10 October 2012, proposed another location for the assembly planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14, namely the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail district, on the outskirts of Baku — the same location proposed by the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) in application no. 76319/13.

At the material time, Article 5 § I of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required any person or persons organising an assembly listed in Article 3 of that Law to notify in advance the relevant body of the executive authority in written form, as a rule at least five days prior to the day of convening the intended assembly, for the purposes of authorising the assembly's time and place and the route of a march.
At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the form of the intended assembly.
At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the general purpose of the assembly.
At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the place and time of convening of the assembly.
At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the approximate number of participants.

At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include, in respect of a march, its proposed route (the place where the march begins, its distance and an end location).

At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the name, surname, patronymic and address of the organisers of the assembly.
At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the date of submission of the written notification.

At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include contact telephone numbers or, in the event of their absence, contact addresses.
At the material time, Article 5 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required all organisers of the assembly to sign the written notification.

At the material time, Article 9 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the relevant body of the executive authority shall allocate in each city and district special areas for conducting gatherings, meetings and demonstrations, and shall publish a list of those proposed places in the local press and bring it to the attention of the population by other means.
At the material time, Article 9 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that organisers may choose one of the places proposed for gatherings, meetings and demonstrations.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted in its letter of 18 April 2012 that the locations indicated by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 were 'areas with intense traffic, and therefore it was not possible to hold assemblies there'.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted in its letter of 18 April 2012 that 'it was not possible to ensure security in respect of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13, considering the serious problems that the assembly would cause to the free movement of citizens who did not want to participate in it, and to the smooth functioning of transport'.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted in its letter of 10 October 2012 that the location indicated by the applicant in application no. 30456/14 was an 'area with intense traffic, and therefore it was not possible to hold assemblies there'.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted in its letter of 10 October 2012 that 'it was not possible to ensure security in respect of the assembly planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14, considering the serious problems that the assembly would cause to the free movement of citizens who did not want to participate in it, and to the smooth functioning of transport'.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) stated in its letter of 18 April 2012 that the assembly proposed by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was 'to no purpose' (keçirilməsi məqsədəuyğun hesab olunmur) because another assembly with a similar cause had already been designated a location on the same day.

The applicants in application no. 76319/13 argued before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 that one of the locations they had proposed — namely, a square in front of the Tabriz cinema in the Nizami district of Baku — was on the Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) indicative list of places for the holding of public assemblies.

The applicants in application no. 76319/13 argued before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 that the location on the outskirts of Baku proposed by the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) — namely, the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail district — was unfit for holding public assemblies.

The applicant in application no. 30456/14 argued before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 that the planned location of the assembly (starting at a square adjacent to Parliament Avenue, following that avenue, and finishing in front of the Parliament building) was very important for the purpose of the assembly, since the demands that the participants intended to voice were related to and addressed to the Parliament.

None of the domestic courts addressed the applicants' argument in application no. 76319/13 that the square in front of the Tabriz cinema in the Nizami district of Baku was on the Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) indicative list of places for the holding of public assemblies.

None of the domestic courts addressed the applicant's argument in application no. 30456/14 that the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) had failed to present any evidence in support of its allegations.

None of the domestic courts addressed the applicants' argument in application no. 76319/13 that the location on the outskirts of Baku proposed by the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) was unfit for holding public assemblies.

None of the domestic courts addressed the applicant's argument in application no. 30456/14 that the planned location of the assembly was very important for the purpose of the assembly because the demands were related to and addressed to the Parliament.
